kept.title: Tests use a private daemon + tmp-dir CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA, never the live :8787 graph
kept.summary: Sandboxed-daemon convention: any test needing a daemon spawns a private one on a random port with a tmp-dir CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA (pattern in test/app-restart.test.js) and must never read or mutate real graph state. Forgetting this corrupts the operator's live :8787 graph.

kept.title: The shipped benchmark is held-out grading: prose spec in, external suite the agent never sees grades it
kept.summary: bench/heldout/ is the only benchmark this repo claims on: the agent solves from a prose spec with NO test/rubric in the worktree, the frozen artifact is graded by an external held-out suite it never saw, and a cold-arm-must-fail guard gates any win claim. The only arm difference is graph access during solve.

kept.title: Memory is load-bearing iff the knowledge is empirical, external-to-artifact, AND project-local
kept.summary: The standing proven claim: retrieved memory lets an agent solve cases it otherwise cannot ONLY when all three hold - (1) empirical (found by running, not derivable from spec), (2) external to the artifact (nothing in-worktree reveals it), (3) project-local (absent from the model's pretraining prior). Violate any one and memory is a null or a tax.

kept.title: Causal win measured at n=2: cold 0/10 and 0/8, warm 8.8/10 and 8/8, warm wrote MORE code
kept.summary: On held-out edge cases the agent never saw, cold scored 0/10 and 0/8 with zero variance; warm scored 8.8/10 and 8/8. Warm wrote 3.8x and 1.7x MORE artifact (citing the seeded note), so the win is retrieve-and-apply (added capability), not shortcutting. These are the actual project-local measured numbers.

kept.title: Winnable-regime frequency on this corpus is ~23% (12/52), resting on project-local facts
kept.summary: Of 52 completed note-dependent tasks, ~23% (12/52) are winnable - the project-local-measured-facts slice, NOT the general-infra slice (pretraining covers that: 0/4 traps survived in Phase 1). Carries an explicit self-similar-corpus caveat: the corpus is the orchestrator benchmarking itself, so the category transfers but not the 23% point estimate.

kept.title: Injection cost = payload size only; the entire ON/OFF gap is cache_read, work never moved
kept.summary: Forced full payload (~25k chars) cost 1.63x ON/OFF; lean payload (~1-3k chars) cost 1.03x. The whole cost difference is cache_read on the injected payload - output tokens (real work) never moved. Lean injection is cost-neutral. Measure work with output_tokens; headline on cost-weighted gross (cache_read bills ~0.1x).

kept.title: Forced context imposes up to ~2x over-deliberation tax; the blocker was never recall
kept.summary: Eight consecutive nulls on self-solvable tasks; forced/precise context only added deliberation (monotone in amount injected, up to ~2x hardness tax - the combined DAG+RAG arm was the WORST). v7 proved semantic retrieval demonstrably worked and changed nothing - recall quality was never the limiter, so don't blame/tune retrieval to chase wins.

kept.title: The oracle leak: an in-worktree test/dependency IS the answer key, so the agent reverse-engineers it
kept.summary: wincase-c's rigging guard did NOT hold - cold solved 3/3 by reading the committed acceptance test, whose generator exposes expected behavior, no matter how strategy-silent the prose spec is. A fully-specified committed test (or dependency source, see silent-cap) for a pure function leaves no empirical gap. This is structural, not a spec-writing flaw - production is naturally held-out, the bench had to be re-engineered to look like it.

kept.title: Bench v1-v7 are contaminated and excluded from the release - make NO claims on them
kept.summary: The first seven ON-vs-OFF benchmark versions shipped their acceptance tests inside the agent's worktree, so every cold baseline overstated self-solvability (caught by the rigging guard on the eighth). v1-v7 are gitignored, excluded from the release, and carry no claims. Only bench/heldout/ ships.

kept.title: Cursor: do NOT also wire the same hook events in .cursor/hooks.json - double execution
kept.summary: When merging adapters/cursor/settings.sample.json into .claude/settings.json, do not additionally wire the same events in .cursor/hooks.json - both fire and the gate/mint hooks run twice. The CLI even emits a warning for the native-.cursor/hooks.json path.

kept.title: When session hooks don't fire, MCP-side daemon refusal on start_task/merge is the backstop
kept.summary: The edit-gate is defense-in-depth: session hooks are the front line, but in harnesses/modes where hooks degrade (Cursor CLI -p, cloud, Codex), the daemon's MCP-side refusal on start_task/merge (rejects a claim with no registered worktree) remains the enforcement backstop. Don't assume removing hooks removes the gate.

kept.title: .graph/** is merge=ours; every clone must run 'git config merge.ours.driver true' once
kept.summary: The daemon is the source of truth for graph state, so .gitattributes assigns '.graph/** merge=ours' - on any merge the current branch's .graph wins wholesale, never content-merged (avoids delete/modify + checkpoint.json conflicts from attempt-branch worktrees). Merge drivers aren't portable, so each fresh clone needs the one-time 'git config merge.ours.driver true' or merges break.

kept.title: The net = gross - plumbing token metric was a retracted artifact of sticky MCP attribution
kept.summary: Early reporting used net tokens and saw ON look like 0.35x ('65% less work') - but attributionMcpServer tagging is sticky across post-call messages, bucketing most of ON's cache_read into 'plumbing'. Pure artifact, retracted. Use output_tokens (or fresh input+output) as the work measure, not net.

kept.title: Bench driver waits must be foreground 'kill -0' polling on the child PID
kept.summary: Three driver-death failure modes cost real runs: macOS has no 'timeout' coreutil (scripts assuming it die silently), detached/background drivers get orphaned and killed, and watching for output files gives FS read-cache false positives. The only reliable wait is foreground 'kill -0' polling on the child PID.
